mainTopic: The three-month waiting period: minors, converts and freed maidservants, רבי יוסי's reasoning, and the meaning of 'כהנות' in the משנה of switched brides
overview: The three-month waiting period before a woman remarries exists so that, if she turns out to be pregnant, we know who the father is. The amud opens by saying the רבנן made even a קטנה wait, because of a גדולה. The גמרא challenges this from the משנה about switched brides, where minors went straight back to their husbands. It answers that switched brides are rare, and the רבנן do not make a גזרה for rare cases. A second version of שמואל's teaching then says a קטנה does not wait at all, because זנות with a minor is rare. It also exempts an adult גיורת and משוחררת, and the גמרא explains that שמואל follows רבי יוסי against רבי יהודה. רבה says רבי יוסי assumes such a woman used an absorbent. אביי rejects this from the case of a maidservant freed suddenly through שן ועין, and from the case of an אנוסה. Instead, אביי explains that the woman turns over to avoid pregnancy, while רבי יהודה worries she did not turn over well enough. Finally, the גמרא works out the משנה's word 'כהנות'. רבא explains it as daughters of כהנים married to ישראלים, who lose their right to eat תרומה in their father's house. The amud closes with the הדרן for פרק אַרְבָּעָה אַחִין.

steps.title: The Rabbis made minors wait because of adults
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the earlier answer: a minor girl involved in זנות must also wait three months, because the רבנן made a גזרה on minors to match the rule for adults.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן decreed that a קטנה must wait, because of a גדולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its earlier answer. A minor cannot get pregnant, but the רבנן still made her wait three months so that people would not mix her up with an adult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the letter of the law there is no reason for a קטנה to wait, because she cannot get pregnant. The wait comes only from a rabbinic גזרה, which keeps the rule the same for every woman. This claim is what the next step attacks.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis made a protective decree

phrases.english: And the Rabbis decreed about a minor because of an adult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from before this piece, about the minor needing to wait.
steps.terutzMaskana: A minor waits three months only because of a גזרה tied to adult women.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה about switched brides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: do we really make a גזרה on minors because of adults? The משנה says minors who cannot give birth go back to their husbands right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really decree on a minor because of an adult? But we learned in the משנה: if they were minors who cannot give birth, we return them right away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks step 1. It quotes a משנה where young girls who could not have children did not have to wait at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה's case, brides were switched by mistake, so the husbands had to separate from them for three months. Minors were sent back at once. If the רבנן really made a גזרה on minors because of adults, the משנה should have made the minors wait too.

keyTerms.meaning: And do we really...? (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: And do we really decree about a minor because of an adult?
But didn't we learn: If they were minors
phrases.notes: This is the משנה about two men whose brides got switched at the wedding.

phrases.english: who are not able to give birth —
we return them immediately.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי גָּזְרִינַן קְטַנָּה מִשּׁוּם גְּדוֹלָה? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the גזרה stated in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רבנן decreed a waiting period for minors because of adults
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lets minors go back immediately, which shows there was no such גזרה.

steps.title: The משנה was a one-time ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל, quoting רב, answers that the משנה's ruling was a הוראת שעה, a special ruling for one time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: it was a ruling for the moment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The משנה's ruling was special to one situation, so it does not show the general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הוראת שעה is a ruling given for an unusual time or situation. We cannot learn a general rule from it, so the גזרה on minors still stands everywhere else.

keyTerms.meaning: A one-time ruling for special circumstances

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
It was a provisional ruling for that time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב: הוֹרָאַת שָׁעָה הָיְתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה shows there is no גזרה on minors.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה was a one-time ruling, so the general גזרה stands.

steps.title: Did it really happen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: calling it a הוראת שעה implies a real event happened, but the משנה reads like a general rule, not a story.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that imply it actually happened?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב's answer. A 'one-time ruling' only makes sense for a real event, and the משנה does not describe one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is written as a general case ('if they were minors'), not as the story of something that happened. So calling it a ruling for a specific moment does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Does that imply that it happened?

phrases.english: By implication, it actually happened?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רב's answer in step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A one-time ruling assumes a real event, but the משנה presents a general case.

steps.title: Like a one-time ruling: switching is rare
steps.stepSummary: The answer is reworded: the משנה is 'like' a הוראת שעה, because switched brides are uncommon, and the רבנן do not make a גזרה for rare cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was like a one-time ruling, and switching is uncommon.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes רב's answer. The משנה is not a real one-time event. It is only like one, because brides almost never get switched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן make a גזרה only for things that happen often. Switched brides are rare, so no גזרה was made for that case, and the minors could return right away. The general גזרה on minors still applies in common situations.
steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן do not make a גזרה for uncommon situations. That is why the minors in the משנה did not wait.

phrases.english: Rather: it was like a provisional ruling.
And switching is uncommon.
phrases.notes: 'Switching' means the brides who were mixed up at the wedding in that משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rewords the answer of step 3 to get around the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording plus the principle that no גזרה is made for rare cases
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is rare, so there is no גזרה there, but the general גזרה on minors stands.

steps.title: Another version of שמואל's teaching
steps.stepSummary: A second version: שמואל said all women wait three months except an adult גיורת and משוחררת, and a minor בת ישראל does not need to wait.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: some say שמואל said: all women must wait three months, except an adult convert and an adult freed maidservant. But a minor Jewish girl does not need to wait three months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of שמואל's teaching. In this version the minor does not wait at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version a minor had to wait because of a גזרה. In this version she is exempt. The adult convert and freed maidservant are also exempt, and the גמרא will soon explain both points.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same teaching continuing. It is a second version that disagrees with the first version about the minor.

phrases.english: Another version, some say it this way:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כּוּלָּן צְרִיכוֹת לְהַמְתִּין שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים,
phrases.english: Shmuel said: All women must wait three months,
except for an adult convert and an adult freed maidservant.
[But] a minor Jewish girl
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets.

phrases.english: does not need to wait three months.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא, אָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a different version of שמואל's teaching from the one behind step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An adult גיורת and משוחררת, and a minor בת ישראל, do not need to wait three months.

steps.title: Which case does שמואל mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the minor's exemption refers to. If it is מיאון, שמואל already said that. If it is a גט, שמואל said she does need to wait.
steps.simpleTranslation: In what case? If by refusal, שמואל already said that once. If by a divorce document, שמואל said she does need to wait, as שמואל said: if she refused him, she does not need to wait three months; if he gave her a גט, she must wait three months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to find which situation שמואל is talking about. It rules out the two obvious options one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A minor's marriage can end with מיאון or with a גט. שמואל already taught that after מיאון there is no wait, so repeating it would be pointless. After a גט he said she must wait, so the exemption cannot be about that.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor's refusal, which ends a rabbinic marriage

phrases.english: In what case?
If by refusal —
but Shmuel already said it one time.

phrases.aramaic: אִי בְּגֵט — הָא קָאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל דְּבָעֲיָא!
phrases.english: If by a divorce document — but Shmuel says that she needs to wait!
As Shmuel said: If she refused him —
she does not need to wait three months!
If he gave her a divorce document —
she must wait three months!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which case step 6's exemption for a minor refers to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the minor left her marriage in שמואל's case: מיאון, גט, or something else.

steps.title: The case is זנות, which is rare for a minor
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's exemption is about a minor involved in זנות. That is uncommon, so the רבנן made no גזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about promiscuity, and promiscuity with a minor is uncommon.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. שמואל is talking about a minor who had relations outside marriage, and that rarely happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same rule as step 5: no גזרה for rare cases. In the first version the רבנן did make a גזרה on a minor in זנות. Here the reasoning is that it is too rare to need one.
steps.whatToRemember: In this second version, a minor does not wait because זנות with a minor is rare, and the רבנן do not make a גזרה for rare cases.

phrases.english: Rather, it is about promiscuity,
and promiscuity with a minor is uncommon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בִּזְנוּת, וּזְנוּת בִּקְטַנָּה לָא שְׁכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7's question after both options there were ruled out.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is זנות, and since that is rare for a minor, there is no גזרה.

steps.title: Why not make converts and freed maidservants wait?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: a גיורת and a משוחררת were often involved in זנות before, so the רבנן should make them wait.
steps.simpleTranslation: A גיורת and a משוחררת, with whom זנות is common: let the רבנן decree that they wait!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about the other exemption in שמואל's teaching. Using the same logic, these women's situation was common, so a גזרה should apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said there is no גזרה because זנות is rare for a minor. The flip side is that where זנות is common, as it was for these women before they converted or were freed, we would expect a waiting period.

phrases.english: A convert and a freed maidservant,
with whom promiscuity is common, let us decree!

steps.triggerLanguage: גִּיּוֹרֶת וּמְשׁוּחְרֶרֶת דִּשְׁכִיחַ בְּהוּ זְנוּת, לִיגְזוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses step 8's reasoning to challenge the exemption of the גיורת and משוחררת in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's exemption for an adult גיורת and משוחררת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a גזרה depends on how common זנות is, these women, for whom it was common, should have to wait.

steps.title: שמואל follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: שמואל ruled like רבי יוסי, who disagrees with רבי יהודה in a ברייתא and lets a convert, captive or maidservant marry right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said it according to רבי יוסי, as it was taught: a convert, a captive and a maidservant who were redeemed, converted or freed must wait three months; this is the view of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי permits them to be betrothed and married immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל follows רבי יוסי. It brings a ברייתא where רבי יוסי says these women do not need to wait.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a מחלוקת in the ברייתא. רבי יהודה requires the three-month wait for these women, and רבי יוסי does not. שמואל simply ruled like רבי יוסי, so his exemption makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who was taken captive
To become betrothed and to marry

phrases.english: He said it according to Rabbi Yosei.
As it was taught: The convert, the captive woman, and the maidservant
who were redeemed, converted, or freed —
must wait three months,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַתִּיר לֵיאָרֵס וְלִינָּשֵׂא מִיָּד.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei permits them to be betrothed and married immediately.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9's challenge by tying שמואל to one side of a ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Tying the ruling to one side of a מחלוקת
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל holds like רבי יוסי, who lets these women marry right away.

steps.title: רבה explains רבי יוסי's reason
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that רבי יוסי holds a woman involved in זנות uses an absorbent so she will not get pregnant, so there is no worry about pregnancy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: what is רבי יוסי's reason? He holds that a woman who is promiscuous uses an absorbent so that she will not become pregnant.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains why רבי יוסי does not require a wait. A woman in זנות takes steps to avoid pregnancy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole point of the three-month wait is to check for pregnancy. If we assume such a woman protected herself from getting pregnant, the wait has no purpose, so she may marry right away.

keyTerms.meaning: A soft absorbent material used to prevent pregnancy

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's first explanation of רבי יוסי is that such a woman protected herself from pregnancy with an absorbent. אביי attacks this in the next step and replaces it in step 14.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the waiting period depends on a real worry about pregnancy. Where that worry is removed, the wait is not needed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי —
phrases.english: Rabba said: What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei?
He holds that a woman who is promiscuous
has relations using an absorbent so that she will not become pregnant.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבי יוסי's view quoted in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי assumes a woman in זנות prevents pregnancy, so no waiting period is needed.

steps.title: אביי asks about a maidservant freed suddenly
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that רבה's absorbent explanation fits a גיורת, שבויה and שפחה who expected to be freed. It does not fit a שפחה freed suddenly through שן ועין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: I understand a convert. Since she plans to convert, she guards herself so that children conceived in holiness can be told apart from children conceived outside it. A captive and a maidservant also hear from their masters that they will be freed, so they guard themselves. But a maidservant who goes free because her master knocked out her tooth or eye: how does your reason work for her?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's explanation of רבי יוסי from Step 11. He shows one case where the absorbent reason cannot work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's reason only works if the woman knew ahead of time that she needed to avoid pregnancy. A שפחה freed through שן ועין had no warning, so she had no reason to use an absorbent. Yet רבי יוסי still seems to let her marry right away.

keyTerms.meaning: A child conceived in holiness, after the conversion
A maidservant set free because her master knocked out her tooth or eye
How can you find it? How does it work?

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: 'To him' means to רבה, whose explanation is in Step 11.

phrases.english: Granted, a female convert,
since her mind is set on converting,
she guards herself,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי לְהַבְחִין בֵּין זֶרַע שֶׁנִּזְרַע בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
phrases.english: in order to tell apart seed sown in holiness
from seed sown not in holiness.
A captive and a maidservant also,
since they hear from their masters,
phrases.notes: They hear that they are about to be ransomed or set free.

phrases.english: they guard themselves.
But one who goes free through a tooth or an eye,
how can you find it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's explanation in Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's explanation that a woman in זנות uses an absorbent
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The absorbent requires advance warning. A שפחה freed by שן ועין had no warning, so the reason fails for her.

steps.title: רבי יוסי does not agree in sudden cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible answer, that רבי יוסי agrees she must wait in sudden cases. A משנה shows רבי יוסי lets even a raped or seduced woman marry right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that whenever it happens on its own, רבי יוסי agrees she must wait: but we learned in a משנה that a woman who was raped or seduced must wait three months, according to רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי lets her get engaged and married immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way to save רבה, then shows from a משנה that this way does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A possible answer is that רבי יוסי only permits women who could plan ahead. But a raped woman could not plan at all, and רבי יוסי still permits her to marry right away. So אביי's question stands, and רבה's absorbent reason cannot be the whole story.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (a possible answer is raised)
A woman who was raped and a woman who was seduced

phrases.english: And if you will say:
wherever it happens by itself, Rabbi Yosei agrees,
phrases.notes: He means רבי יוסי would agree she has to wait, since she had no chance to protect herself.

phrases.english: but didn't we learn:
a woman who was raped and one who was seduced
must wait three months,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַתִּיר לֵיאָרֵס וְלִינָּשֵׂא מִיָּד.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei permits her to be betrothed and married immediately.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: כֹּל דְּמִמֵּילָא מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a possible defense against the question in Step 12
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that רבי יוסי agrees she must wait in unplanned cases
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוסי permits an אנוסה to marry immediately, even though she could not have planned anything

steps.title: אביי's new reason: she turns over
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a new reason for רבי יוסי: a woman in זנות turns over after relations so she will not become pregnant.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: A woman who has forbidden relations turns over afterward so that she will not become pregnant.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רבה's reason did not work, אביי offers a different explanation for רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Turning over is something a woman can do right after relations, with no advance planning. So it works even for a שפחה freed suddenly, and even for an אנוסה. This replaces רבה's absorbent reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (an earlier idea is dropped and a new one given)
A woman who has forbidden relations

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the accepted reason for רבי יוסי's view in this סוגיא.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
A woman who has forbidden relations
turns over so that she will not become pregnant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבה's reason, which failed in Steps 12-13
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reasoning replaces the earlier explanation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי relies on an absorbent, which needs planning ahead
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי relies on the woman turning over afterward, which needs no planning

steps.title: What about רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if women turn over to avoid pregnancy, why does רבי יהודה still make them wait?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other opinion, how does he explain it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה deals with אביי's reason. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If turning over prevents pregnancy, there seems to be no reason to wait three months. So the גמרא needs to explain why רבי יהודה still requires waiting.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one, the opposing opinion

phrases.english: And the other?
phrases.notes: 'The other' is רבי יהודה, who says she must wait three months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the other side responds to אביי's reason
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יהודה requires waiting if women turn over to avoid pregnancy

steps.title: Maybe she did not turn over well
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה worries that she may not have turned over well enough, so she might be pregnant.
steps.simpleTranslation: We worry that maybe she did not turn over well enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of Step 15. רבי יהודה agrees she turns over, but he does not fully trust it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree a woman in זנות tries to avoid pregnancy. They argue only about whether we rely on that: רבי יוסי does, and רבי יהודה worries it may not have worked.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי lets these women marry right away because a woman in זנות turns over to avoid pregnancy. רבי יהודה makes them wait three months because maybe she did not turn over well enough.

phrases.english: We are concerned
that perhaps she did not turn over well enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָיְישִׁינַן שֶׁמָּא לֹא נִתְהַפְּכָה יָפֶה יָפֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה worries the turning over may not have worked well enough

steps.title: Why does the משנה say only 'daughters of priests'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about switched brides: 'if they were כהנות'. It asks whether that means only כהנות are disqualified from תרומה and not ישראליות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And if they were כהנות, etc.' Does that mean only daughters of כהנים, but not daughters of ישראלים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה about two brides who were switched at the חופה, and challenges the wording 'כהנות'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Losing the right to eat תרומה is about being married to a כהן, not about whose daughter she is. A בת ישראל married to a כהן also eats תרומה, so she should lose it too. So the word 'כהנות' seems too narrow.

keyTerms.meaning: Daughters of ישראלים, women who are not from a כהן family
Etc., the rest of the line in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new topic. The discussion about waiting three months is finished. Now the גמרא is back to the משנה about two brides who were switched at the חופה.

phrases.english: 'And if they were daughters of priests, etc.'
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on to say they become disqualified from eating תרומה.

phrases.english: Daughters of priests, yes,
daughters of Israelites, no?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם הָיוּ כֹּהֲנוֹת כּוּ׳. כֹּהֲנוֹת — אִין, יִשְׂרְאֵלִיּוֹת — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A בת ישראל married to a כהן also eats תרומה, so limiting the rule to daughters of כהנים makes no sense.

steps.title: Read it as 'wives of priests'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording: read the משנה as 'if they were wives of כהנים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'If they were wives of כהנים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the משנה so that it is about women married to כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading it as 'wives of כהנים' fits the rule, because a woman eats תרומה through her husband. Now it includes a בת ישראל married to a כהן.

phrases.english: Say:
'If they were wives of priests.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording problem of Step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about daughters of כהנים
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about wives of כהנים

steps.title: Wives of priests, but not wives of Israelites?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new reading: does it mean only wives of כהנים are affected, and not wives of ישראלים?
steps.simpleTranslation: Wives of כהנים, yes; wives of ישראלים, no?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the new wording from Step 18. Step 20 gives the source behind this challenge, and רבא answers it in Step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only wives of כהנים are mentioned, it sounds like wives of ישראלים lose nothing, even though each woman had relations with a man who was not her husband. The גמרא finds that hard to accept, so the new wording is now being questioned too.

keyTerms.meaning: Wives of ישראלים, men who are not כהנים

phrases.english: Wives of priests, yes,
wives of Israelites, no?

steps.triggerLanguage: נְשֵׁי כֹהֲנִים — אִין, נְשֵׁי יִשְׂרְאֵלִים — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the new wording given in Step 18
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Naming only wives of כהנים suggests wives of ישראלים lose nothing, and the גמרא finds that hard to accept.

steps.title: Proof that a ישראל's wife is also disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its challenge. רב עמרם quotes רב ששת: a raped wife of a ישראל stays permitted to her husband but is disqualified from כהונה. So the switched brides who were married to ישראלים should also be affected.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב עמרם say: רב ששת told us this, and he showed us it comes from a משנה: the wife of a ישראל who was raped is still permitted to her husband, but she is disqualified from marrying into כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its challenge against the new wording 'wives of כהנים'. It brings a teaching that shows wives of ישראלים are also hurt by forbidden relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new wording made it sound as if only wives of כהנים lose something. But רב ששת teaches that a wife of a ישראל who had forbidden relations against her will becomes disqualified from כהונה, even though her own marriage stays fine. So the switched brides married to ישראלים should also be included, and the new wording leaves them out.

keyTerms.meaning: He lit up our eyes (he showed us clearly)
The wife of a regular Jew (not a כהן)

steps.confusionAlert: She stays permitted to her own husband. The disqualification only matters later, for example if she is widowed and wants to marry a כהן.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Amram say:

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִילְּתָא אֲמַר לַן רַב שֵׁשֶׁת,
phrases.english: This matter Rav Sheshet told us,
and he lit up our eyes from the Mishnah:
phrases.notes: He means רב ששת showed them that this rule can be learned from a משנה.

phrases.english: The wife of an Israelite who was raped,
even though she is permitted to her husband,
is disqualified from the priesthood.
phrases.notes: So if her husband dies, she may not marry a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that gives the challenge in step 19 its force.
steps.kashyaTarget: The changed wording 'wives of כהנים' from step 18.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב ששת shows that a ישראל's wife who had forbidden relations is also disqualified from כהונה. The new wording wrongly leaves wives of ישראלים out.

steps.title: רבא: daughters of כהנים married to ישראלים
steps.stepSummary: רבא keeps the original word 'כהנות'. He explains that it means daughters of כהנים married to ישראלים. Because of the forbidden relations, they lose the right to go back and eat תרומה in their father's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is what the משנה means. If they were daughters of כהנים married to ישראלים, they are disqualified from eating תרומה in their family's house.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new answer. He goes back to the original word 'כהנות' and explains what loss these women suffer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, a כהן's daughter married to a ישראל may go back to eating תרומה in her father's house if her husband dies and she has no children. The forbidden relations take away that right. So the משנה is not saying that wives of ישראלים are unaffected. It is pointing out a special loss for כהנות married to ישראלים.

keyTerms.meaning: Of their family's house (their father's household)

steps.whatToRemember: The original wording 'כהנות' stays. It refers to daughters of כהנים married to ישראלים, who lose the chance to return to תרומה in their father's house.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer solves both problems at once. It explains why the משנה mentions כהנות, and it no longer seems to leave anyone out.

phrases.english: Rava said: This is what it is saying:
If they were daughters of priests
married to an Israelite,
they are disqualified from the teruma of their family's house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from steps 19-20 by dropping the changed wording and explaining the original one differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reading 'wives of כהנים' (step 18) seemed to say that wives of ישראלים lose nothing, which contradicts רב ששת's teaching.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כהנות' means daughters of כהנים married to ישראלים, who lose the right to return to תרומה in their father's house.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק אַרְבָּעָה אַחִין
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula of the פרק 'אַרְבָּעָה אַחִין'.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק אַרְבָּעָה אַחִין.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the פרק אַרְבָּעָה אַחִין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not a legal statement. It is the traditional way of finishing a פרק, expressing the hope to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: Four Brothers (the name of this פרק)

phrases.english: We will return to you, Four Brothers

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after רבא's answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק אַרְבָּעָה אַחִין is complete.
